articles.title: DREAMFORCE PROMISED AN AGENTIC CRM. LIGHTFIELD HAS ALREADY BUILT IT
articles.summary:
Today's most popular CRM is a database with a UI. But the companies of the future are agent-first, and agents need more context. They need a world model of your business.

Lightfield [5] is the CRM engineered for the future [6]. It updates itself from every call, email, meeting, and Slack thread, and connects everything to the people, deals, and accounts they changed.

Lightfield agents find prospects that look like your best customers, book the meetings, capture action items, diagnose your funnel - and learn from your best sellers to codify what works.

✅ 5,000+ companies signed up in 10 months.

✅ $47M Series A from a16z.

articles.title: THE HARNESS MARGIN OPPORTUNITY
articles.summary: The right harness can cut the cost of the same result by 71% without a loss of accuracy. This presents an opportunity for the next generation of software applications. State-of-the-art models can be expensive to use, but a good harness can reduce costs enough for them to be a viable option. An effective harness requires deep customer understanding, a collection of relevant evals, and a factory for automating hill-climbing.

articles.title: THE NEW KINGMAKERS
articles.summary: Revenue scale is no longer sufficient when raising a round. What actually matters is how many top AI-native companies use, love, and embrace your products and profess undying loyalty to you. AI-native companies are the hardest customers to win, so they are the leading indicator. Revenue can be bought, but loyalty from a kingmaker can't be manufactured.

articles.title: PULLEY, A CARTA RIVAL, IS SHUTTING DOWN
articles.summary: Pulley raised more than $50M to compete with Carta. Now it's shutting down and directing customers to that same competitor. The cap-table startup closes December 8, giving customers about twelve weeks to move. A former employee speculated that spreadsheets, increasingly improved with AI, were a bigger competitive problem than Carta itself. If you use Pulley, start checking the migration details now, especially which records transfer automatically and what you'll need to export yourself.

articles.title: INSIDE 12 MONTHS OF AI SEARCH EXPERIMENTS
articles.summary: HubSpot spent twelve months testing what gets a company found in AI search. Adding an llms.txt file did nothing, while 92% of its highly specific industry and use-case pages eventually earned citations. A page-speed overhaul increased AI crawler visits by 1,600%, and qualified leads from AI search rose 1,850% over the year. The experiments give teams somewhere concrete to start. Track whether the content brings qualified leads, though, because more crawler visits alone won't tell you whether it's working.

articles.title: WHY WOULD SOMEONE PAY FOR YOUR APP WHEN AI DOES IT FOR FREE?
articles.summary: Your customer can ask ChatGPT for a lesson. Getting them to practice again tomorrow is a different problem. This article suggests comparing your app's main use case with what someone can do in a blank chat window, then looking at what's missing. Does your app remember their progress, organize what comes next, or give them someone to practice with? Those are reasons to keep using it even when the answers are available elsewhere. If you're struggling to explain why someone should pay, try the comparison yourself.

articles.title: REACH 8 MILLION TECH PROFESSIONALS READING TLDR
articles.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach developers, PMs, marketers, founders and other tech leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities [13].

articles.title: MERCURY BOOKS
articles.summary: Mercury Books brings AI-powered accounting to Mercury. It can generate P&L, cash flow, and balance sheet reports using Mercury data and data from external financial platforms. The product was co-designed alongside accountants from leading firms. Existing Mercury customers can get started with Books in minutes.

articles.title: COLUMN IS RELEASING FOUR NEW PRODUCTS
articles.summary: USDC and USDT are now completely interoperable with the US dollar and every underlying US and international payment rail on Column. Column has built its own card issuer processor, allowing its customers to launch and run card programs with one integration. Column customers can now issue US dollar accounts and cards to verified customers globally. They can also receive, hold, and send foreign currencies in individually numbered accounts with connections to international instant payment systems like SEPA Instant.

articles.title: REIMAGINING ADVERTISING WITH AI
articles.summary: A customer can now ask an ad questions before visiting your website. OpenAI is testing Sponsored Agents with select US advertisers, letting users talk with a business-sponsored agent before clicking through to buy. It's also adding ChatGPT Ads integrations to HubSpot and Shopify. That moves some of the selling into the ad itself. If you get access to the test, your product information and the agent's answers will need as much attention as the creative and landing page.

articles.title: PULLEY IS “WINDING DOWN” | WHAT HAPPENED?
articles.summary: Many founders are getting tired right now. They raised and built in a pre-AI world. Many want to build something else for a post-AI world. This can be a big opportunity for many companies that are in a strong financial position.

articles.title: WHY DOES YOUR TEAM THINK YOU'RE A WORSE MANAGER THAN YOU DO?
articles.summary: You suggest a new feature during a meeting. A week later, someone has built it, and the project you actually needed is behind. You thought you were sharing an idea, but they thought you were giving them a task. This is one reason founders and their teams can disagree about how well things are managed. Tell people whether you're asking for opinions or assigning work. When you do add a task, explain how it ranks against what they're already doing.

articles.title: HOW TO RAISE VENTURE CAPITAL CHAPTER 1: THE SPEED RUN
articles.summary: One investor wants an answer by Friday. Another can't meet until next month. You can end up choosing before you know who else is interested. This fundraising guide explains how to avoid that by building relationships early, then scheduling your pitch meetings close together so investors can reach decisions around the same time. Aim to finish the raise before you're down to six months of cash. Even after you accept a term sheet, investors still need to complete their checks and finalize the paperwork before the money reaches your account.

articles.title: THE MOST IMPORTANT PRODUCT DECISION IS WHAT YOU DON'T BUILD
articles.summary: Be extremely choosy about what you add to a system and be militant about taking things out.

articles.title: THE CURATION PROBLEM
articles.summary: AI accelerates product development, but teams risk prioritizing speed over meaningful outcomes, leading to feature bloat.

articles.title: MAXIMIZING RETURN-ON-FEEDBACK
articles.summary: When you let it be known that someone gave you feedback, and they see how you accepted and thanked the person who gave it, you normalize the behavior and make it safer for others to do the same.
